name: Hangrowl
description: Its sleeping posture builds astonishing upper-body strength while leaving the rest of its body slow and comparatively frail. Heavy claws peel bark, dig roots, and tear into anthills. Abrasion can create a bark-like outer layer on one or both forearms, depending on where it rests. Despite its relaxed image, Hangrowl barely recognizes familiar people and cannot remember faces.

name: Swoleth
description: Swoleth uses its massive arms to carry itself through the rainforest and hang beneath sturdy branches like a living anchor. Anchoring one arm and swinging the other gives it enough momentum to crush stonework and hardwood logs. Its legs struggle beneath its upper body, and repeated meetings with the same person often leave it visibly bewildered.

name: Gloomquito
description: Most people are horrified upon learning of this Fakemon's existence. Arriving at night, it often strikes unsuspecting victims to feed. After a meal, its glassy abdomen resembles a round vial filled with dark-red liquid. It was once believed that Gloomquito could drain toxins from poisoned individuals. Thankfully, that medical malpractice has since been corrected. Most deaths associated with this Fakemon result from the diseases it may introduce rather than its bites themselves, but it is nevertheless equal parts annoying and dangerous. Most consider Gloomquito Demonic. Surely this is projection based on its real harms and alarming size, rather than anything to do with the Fakemon's intentions.

name: Vamprick
description: Vamprick senses sleeping prey from the rhythm of its breathing. Unlike Gloomquito, it takes only a small amount of blood from each target. This is not restraint; it is simply easily distracted by the next vulnerable creature it notices. Inarguably twisted, Vamprick seems to enjoy biting the helpless just enough to make them miserable. Several crusades have declared the species eradicated, but isolated nests are still rarely found at elevations above 3,000 feet, in places untouched by sunlight. Report all sightings to state agencies immediately. Do not attempt heroics. Under no circumstances should you let one see you.

name: Croacoa
description: Croacoa's throat pouch produces a sweetly floral gas with unusual restorative effects on skin. In concentrated form, however, the gas becomes dangerously toxic—and Croacoa can ignite it with heat generated inside its body. Carefully diluted Croacoa gas is prized in perfumes and expensive skin treatments. The frilled sensory organs on its head help it measure airflow, temperature, and the resonance of its surroundings. Croacoa uses this information to produce surprisingly intricate melodies while releasing luminous bubbles of perfumed gas. Its performances are occasionally interrupted by an involuntary burp that ignites the nearest bubble. Most Trainers consider this endearing, provided nothing important catches fire.

name: Flambian
description: Flambian illuminates tropical nights with elaborate displays of flame, perfumed smoke, and resonant song. Despite the dangerous materials involved, its performances are graceful and astonishingly precise. Streams of burning alkaloids curl through the air like ribbons, each shaped by the rhythm of its expanding throat pouch. These displays are not courtship or entertainment. Flambian performs to announce that the surrounding territory is occupied—and that it fears no predator within it. Its showmanship should never be mistaken for harmlessness. Researchers continue to debate what might successfully hunt a Flambian. No one has volunteered to test the leading theories.

name: Paratweet
description: Paratweet calls from the canopy in soothing melodies associated with reduced stress and improved recovery. It encourages dormant flowers to open, yet favors gardens vigorous enough to bloom without help. Its beauty inspires companionship, but it demands enormous healthy territory and may abandon Trainers whose gardens fail its expectations.

name: Paradisia
description: Paradisia's wings leave floral afterimages, and it appears capable of remaining airborne indefinitely. Ancient cultures credited it with endless flowers, abundant harvests, and renewed vitality. Scientists dismiss claims that training one preserves youth, yet its long-term Trainers show unusual health and cultivated land within its territory has never suffered a failed harvest.

name: Phaloa
description: Crowned with petals, sepals and leaves, Phaloa's beauty is alluring. Trainers can read the thoughts of the Fakemon if they are allowed to hold the bud at the end of their vining tendrils. They carry themselves through the air, effortlessly floating, as if gravity has no effect on their bodies. Despite it's appearance, both its central eye and many petals are remarkably hard to injure, and that's assuming one can manage to get past it's unusual precognition abilities first. People often fail to understand their alien cognition. Those who raise them from a Keklid however, find a kindred spirit behind the bloom. They are most vigorous in the afternoons, as it appears solar energy feeds their metabolism directly. Despite this, they still search out and devour mycelium. Is the fungal consumption just habit? Or is eating fungi merely seen as something similar to pleasure for them?

name: Scorcaw
description: Proud, exotic Fakemon, much more cognizant of their offensive potential. This makes them both more predictable and more dangerous. Highly social and intelligent, Scorcaw begin to form their system of values based off their trainer or flock. They square up against anything perceived to be a threat to those values. The stronger the opponent, the more resolute Scorcaw becomes, and the hotter it's flames burn. Sizzling and scoring, there is no material known to science that is truly immune to their flaming strikes. This combination produces an equal parts intelligent, dangerous and valiant Fakemon, owing to it's popularity in cultural imagery despite it's rarity. But despite all this, they still love those spicy peppers, and are a Scorchick at heart.

name: Serafin
description: These rare wonders are thought to occur when an Angelic being blesses a Sylvafin. Their radiance can no longer be described as ordinary light alone. It appears to interact with the fabric of reality itself. They particularly love to use these abilities to control water, bending it to fulfill their intentions. This would be frightening, but the Fakemon seems to possess an unusually strong sense of understanding consequences. Where the wisdom comes from, however, is an alarming unknown that biology cannot explain. Serafin typically grow highly attached to their trainers or mates, to the point where willingly abandoning a bonded companion is incomprehensible to them. Don't let the gentle presence deceive you however, they do not fear conflict, and are more than equipped to handle the worst of it.

name: Junrift
description: Believed to share ancestry with the earliest plants, Junrift is described in ancient accounts as a species forged near the beginning of creation to cultivate the natural order. It moves through the forest with an unmistakable rhythm. Slow. Inevitable. Certain. Wherever it settles, exhausted soils recover, fungal networks spread, and plant life flourishes. A trained Junrift can gradually transform even dry valleys into thriving ecosystems. Early peoples worshipped them as gods after witnessing their strange cognition and mastery over life. Recent observations suggest something stranger: Junrift do not consider themselves rulers of nature at all. They appear to recognize humanity as fellow stewards, entrusted alongside them with its cultivation.

name: Pyravion
description: It burns bright, hot and true. The more powerful a foe, the more carefully Pyravion studies its intentions. It rarely challenges the weak, but becomes almost impossible to intimidate when confronting a dangerous aggressor. As it soars through the sky, it may light up the midnight dark like it was day with the amount of light its flames can produce. It frequently ends up at odds with dragons for this reason, and even they fear the sound of a Pyravion. Every once in a while, a dragon will attempt to solve the problem with force and rises to challenge Pyravion. No reliably documented challenge has ended in the dragon's favor. Pyravion can activate and deactivate its flames at will, careful to not burn down the rainforest below with their incredible heat. In folk legends, there have been many stories of mighty warriors that have ridden Pyravion into battle against mythical dragons and titans. Even now the Fakemon are important symbols of strength, vitality and courage in popular literature.

name: Celestraal
description: Few beings are as equally parts good and unsettling as the mighty Celestraal. Winged fish-like angelic beings, they can glide up to space, presumably visiting Heaven, before returning to their watery abodes below. If dark forces or malicious intent are discovered, Celestraal may intervene as a last response. Historically, they are proven to be a very effective last response. It is believed that this Fakemon, more than any other, is responsible for maintaining the life and culture of this realm, and it has proven to be more useful at deterring external or demonic threats than any military could realistically be. Celestraal is also reported to have performed miracles or blessings to those who honor their bonds and act with true sincerity. Thankfully, Celestraal is not looking for moral perfection, but rather, looking for moral honesty and formation. Modern religious imagery borrows shapes inherited from the patterns Celestraal makes with water and light. Nobody actually knows what these patterns mean.
